purpose: Resolve the selected cross-sectional-dispersion concept into one exact no-value mechanism and challenge it against terminal and prospective families before any Campaign031 source partition, dispersion benchmark value, candidate value, comparison value, daily price, or forward return is opened.

selected_mechanism.name: intraday_market_dispersion_decoupling_238m
selected_mechanism.formula: negative population PearsonCorr(abs(stock_return), sqrt(population variance of all other valid stock returns at the same date and return position)) over exactly 238 within-half return positions
selected_mechanism.economic_hypothesis: A higher value means the stock's absolute one-minute movement is less synchronized with broad leave-one-out cross-sectional return dispersion, representing lower exposure to market-wide liquidity fragmentation that may improve resilience from the next open through the third close.
selected_mechanism.return_grid: Form exactly 119 adjacent natural-log close returns inside each 120-close half at 09:31-11:30 and 13:01-15:00, yielding 238 fixed positions. Exclude standalone 09:30 and the lunch transition.
selected_mechanism.benchmark_population_rule: A stock-day contributes its complete 238-element return vector to the same-date benchmark only when all 238 returns are finite. For every date and position accumulate float64 return_sum, float64 return_sum_squares, and integer valid_stock_count in lexicographically sorted symbol order over the accepted joint-clean stock-day key grid.
selected_mechanism.leave_one_out_rule: At every fixed position subtract the stock return from return_sum, its exact square from return_sum_squares, and one from valid_stock_count. Require at least 50 remaining stocks at every position.
selected_mechanism.dispersion_rule: For every position compute the leave-one-out population variance as return_sum_squares/n minus (return_sum/n)^2, without Bessel correction. Canonicalize a negative variance to exact zero only when it is at least -1e-18; a variance below -1e-18 is invalid. Take the nonnegative square root. Retain exact-zero dispersion values at their fixed positions.
selected_mechanism.correlation_rule: Compute one equal-position-weight population Pearson correlation between the complete 238-element absolute stock-return vector and complete 238-element leave-one-out dispersion vector. Require strictly positive population variance in both vectors.
selected_mechanism.direction_rule: Multiply the exact population correlation by negative one once so higher means lower magnitude-dispersion coupling. Do not use absolute correlation, one-minus-correlation, beta, residuals, ranks, signs, thresholds, or subwindows.
selected_mechanism.zero_rule: Retain every exact-zero stock return as exact-zero magnitude and every exact-zero leave-one-out dispersion at its fixed position without removal, bridging, replacement, tolerance reclassification, or sign conditioning.
selected_mechanism.endpoint_rule: Canonicalize the final correlation only when it lies within 1e-12 beyond -1 or +1 before applying the exact negative-one direction transform; otherwise a nonfinite or out-of-range score is missing.
selected_mechanism.missing_rule: Any invalid close-return grid, insufficient leave-one-out peer position, materially negative leave-one-out variance, nonfinite magnitude or dispersion, nonpositive population variance in either complete 238-element vector, invalid correlation, nonfinite score, or score outside [-1,1] makes the stock-day missing; never fill, statistically clip, repair, or substitute.

overlap_challenges.reason: Campaign029 correlates stock absolute returns with the absolute leave-one-out cross-sectional mean return, a common directional shock magnitude. Campaign031 correlates them with the leave-one-out cross-sectional population standard deviation, which can change while the market mean is fixed and measures breadth fragmentation rather than common direction.

Campaign030 retains signed stock and market-mean returns and subtracts two half-session correlations. Campaign031 discards stock signs only after constructing returns, uses cross-sectional dispersion rather than a mean path, and computes one pooled fixed-support correlation.

Market-idiosyncratic share fits a signed stock exposure to the leave-one-out mean return and measures residual-to-total variance. Campaign031 fits no signed beta or residual and instead measures whether stock magnitude co-moves with cross-sectional dispersion through time.

Campaign026 conditions signed stock-market dependence on positive versus negative mean-market states. Campaign031 never conditions on market sign and its external state is nonnegative cross-sectional dispersion.
Campaign021 compares stock-lead and stock-lag signed correlations. Campaign031 uses only synchronous same-position magnitudes and has no lead or lag.

Return-variance entropy is an unordered concentration statistic of the stock's own squared returns. Campaign031 preserves each fixed position and asks whether absolute stock returns align with an independently constructed leave-one-out cross-sectional dispersion path.
Campaign028 correlates the stock's adjacent absolute returns with each other. Campaign031 has no own-return lag and relates each magnitude only to a same-minute external dispersion state.

Market amount-profile synchronization uses normalized turnover allocation and a leave-one-out amount profile. Campaign031 reads no amount or volume and measures cross-sectional close-return dispersion.
Candidate49 measures causal cumulative-VWAP crossings from close, volume, and amount. Campaign031 reads no volume or amount and has no cumulative VWAP or crossing count.
Campaign031 contains one new close-plus-dispersion statistic and no range center of mass, terminal factor value, fitted transform, filter, model, combination, or Campaign030 rescue.

design_choices_frozen_before_values.formula_family: negative synchronous population correlation of stock absolute return and leave-one-out cross-sectional population return dispersion
